atlas_anomaly.comparison_unit: parent-child process relationship and command context.

atlas_anomaly.deviation: an otherwise common binary forms a rare edge or conditional combination.

strategies.name: Detection of Proxy Execution via Trusted Signed Binaries Across Platforms

analytics.name: Analytic 0226
analytics.guidance: Execution of trusted, Microsoft-signed binaries such as `rundll32.exe`, `msiexec.exe`, or `regsvr32.exe` used to execute externally hosted, unsigned, or suspicious payloads through command-line parameters or network retrieval.

tuning.description: Used to profile unexpected parent-child relationships (e.g., regsvr32.exe not launched by explorer.exe)
List of known signed binaries allowed for execution (e.g., msiexec.exe, regsvr32.exe)
Regex to match suspicious arguments, such as URLs, script paths, or DLL entrypoints
Filter to suppress activity contacting legitimate enterprise domains

analytics.name: Analytic 0227
analytics.guidance: Execution of trusted system binaries (e.g., `split`, `tee`, `bash`, `env`) used in uncommon sequences or chained behaviors to execute malicious payloads or perform actions inconsistent with normal system or script behavior.

tuning.description: Binaries like `split`, `tee`, `env`, `awk`, `gzip`, often used in benign scripts
Outlier model for process tree and command arguments

analytics.name: Analytic 0228
analytics.guidance: Use of system binaries such as `osascript`, `bash`, or `curl` to download or execute unsigned code or files in conjunction with application proxying.

tuning.description: Used to detect proxy execution from signed binary to unsigned payload
